4. The pre-emptee-respondent Nos. 2 to 5 appeared in that miscellaneous case and filed written objection challenging the claim of pre-emption. The opposite party No. 23, namely, Abul Kashem filed an application on 24.06.1999 praying for being added as co-preemptor under section 96(4) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act stating, inter-alias that he was a co-sharer by inheritance of the case holding. But the said application was rejected by the order dated 24.06.1999 on the ground that the date of knowledge of the applicant about the case transfer was not mentioned in that application. The opposite party No. 23 then filed another application on 07.07.1999 under section 94(4) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act stating his date of knowledge about the case transfer and prayed for review of the earlier order dated 24.06.1999 and the same application was allowed by the order dated 09.08.1999 and the opposite party No. 23 was made co-petitioner. 

 10. Mr. Khair Azaz Masud, the learned advocate has mainly argued that in this case there is concurrent findings of both the trial court and the lower appellate court that the co-preemptor failed to prove his date of knowledge about the case transfer and in the circumstances the High Court Division committed grave error of law in allowing the preemption of part of the land transferred in favour of the co-preemptor. The learned advocate, has submitted also that in this case the trial court rejected the application of the opposite party No. 23 for being transposed as co-pre-emptor on the finding that the application was barred by limitation and in the circumstances the trial court committed great error and illegality in allowing the same application of this opposite party No. 23 at a subsequent stage and thereafter allowing pre-emption of half of the land transferred in favour of this co-preemptor. The learned advocate has argued that since the trial court earlier rejected the same application for being transposed as co-preemptor there was no scope for the trial court to add this opposite party No. 23 as a co-pre-emptor at a subsequent stage. The learned advocate has contended that since the trial court found the co-preemptor's application under section 96(4) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act time barred he was not entitled to get preemption of the case land and in the circumstances the trial court committed wrong and illegality in allowing the pre-emption of half of the land transferred in favour of this co-preemptor. 

 "II. Because the High Court Division committed error in law in not affirming the appellate court's view that the application of the co-preemptor was filed beyond time as prescribed under section 96(4) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act." 

 "III. Because the High Court. Division committed error in law in not considering that from the evidence of the P.W.1 along with P.W.4 and exhibit-4 the certificate together with material statements of O.P.W. 1 in cross-examination it is proved beyond doubt that service in the preemption case was made on 04.04.1999 in accordance of Civil Procedure Code for the purpose of application of limitation as per section 96(4) of the Act."
